inputs.original_text: Bloomberg: “Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.” “Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]
inputs.modified_text: Bloomberg’s framing is the tell: as rising energy prices, canceled flights, and death and destruction lead people worldwide to ask when the Iran war will stop, Israel is portrayed as uniquely willing to keep going. That contrast recasts continuation as “public resolve” and obscures the interests that may be sustaining it. The account also cuts off after “until,” leaving the central question hanging: who benefits from keeping this war going?
